title: An Evaluation of Chilling Models for Estimating Rest Requirements of Highbush Blueberries
authors: Norvell, D.J.; Moore, J.N.
journal_or_institution: Journal of the American Society for Horticultural Science 107(1):54-56
measured_variables: Rest completion under chill exposures
main_supported_claim: Blueberry chill response was not fully represented by simple hours below 7.2C or classic Utah weights; 1C and 12C were effective but less than 6C
reported_effect_direction: Chill effectiveness peaked near tested 6C; modified model performed more predictably
reported_effect_size_if_available: Treatment/model comparison; no universal cultivar threshold
limitations: Two cultivars and study conditions; does not select a global chilling model
applicability_to_our_model: Blueberry-specific caution on chill model portability
do_not_generalize_beyond: All cultivars, warm-climate protected systems, or evergreen genotypes

title: A Model for Estimating the Completion of Rest for Redhaven and Elberta Peach Trees
authors: Richardson, E.A.; Seeley, S.D.; Walker, D.R.
measured_variables: Temperature response and rest completion
main_supported_claim: Weighted effective chill units can represent temperature-dependent rest completion in the studied peach cultivars
reported_effect_size_if_available: Published response curve; parameter scope is peach
limitations: Cross-species standard-method source only; no blueberry-specific validation
applicability_to_our_model: Utah model algorithm lineage, not blueberry parameter authority
do_not_generalize_beyond: Blueberry-specific chill requirement or production default

title: The Temperature Dependence of Dormancy Breaking in Plants: Mathematical Analysis of a Two-Step Model Involving a Cooperative Transition
authors: Fishman, S.; Erez, A.; Couvillon, G.A.
measured_variables: Two-step precursor/product model
main_supported_claim: Dynamic chill model represents chill accumulation as a two-step temperature-dependent process with intermediate state
reported_effect_direction: Warm-temperature effects depend on process history
reported_effect_size_if_available: Model equations and fitted kinetic constants
limitations: Not a blueberry or evergreen validation
applicability_to_our_model: Selectable generic chilling-algorithm prior and state equation
do_not_generalize_beyond: Blueberry cultivar thresholds or an assertion of release without observation

title: The Temperature-Dependence of Dormancy Breaking in Plants: Computer Simulation of Processes Studied under Controlled Temperatures
authors: Fishman, S.; Erez, A.; Couvillon, G.A.
experiment_duration: Model simulation across controlled thermal regimes
measured_variables: Dynamic model thermal response
main_supported_claim: Dynamic Model reproduces history-dependent chill formation and negation in simulated temperature regimes
reported_effect_size_if_available: Model behavior under specified thermal cycles
limitations: Not blueberry-specific validation; prior constants are not production values

title: Photoperiod and Temperature Treatments Affect Vegetative and Reproductive Growth of an Everbearing Blueberry Genotype
authors: Benevenute et al.
sample_size_if_known: Not reported in article metadata reviewed
management_intervention: Photoperiod (8, 12, 16 h and night interruption) x temperature
measured_variables: Bud initiation, vegetative growth, dormancy behavior
main_supported_claim: FL16-64 initiated buds across tested treatments and some inflorescences bypassed endodormancy; Arcadia response differed

title: Photoperiod and Temperature Effects on Growth and Carbohydrate Storage in Southern Highbush Blueberry Interspecific Hybrid
authors: Spann, T.M.; Williamson, J.G.; Darnell, R.L.

title: Flower Bud Density Affects Vegetative and Fruit Development in Field-Grown Southern Highbush Blueberry
authors: Maust, B.E.; Williamson, J.G.; Darnell, R.L.

title: Pruning Severity Affects Yield, Berry Weight, and Hand Harvest Efficiency of Highbush Blueberry

title: Summer Pruning Differentiates Vegetative Buds to Flower Buds in the Rabbiteye Blueberry (Vaccinium virgatum Ait.)

title: Effect of Source/Sink Ratio on Leaf and Fruit Traits of Blueberry Fruiting Canes in the Field

title: Analysis of Highbush Blueberry Fruit Growth with Exponential Mixed Models
authors: Godoy, C.; Monterubbianesi, G.; Tognetti, J.
management_intervention: Repeated fruit diameter and nonlinear curve fits
measured_variables: Fruit-growth curves
main_supported_claim: Growth commonly showed a double-sigmoid; fitted pattern and clarity varied by cultivar, with Gompertz II best among tested mixed models
reported_effect_size_if_available: Two years, three cultivars
limitations: Selected cultivars and cool-temperate site; curve-fit result is not universal
applicability_to_our_model: Double-sigmoid structure and comparison of candidate curve families

title: Fruit Development Period of Several Southern Highbush Blueberry Cultivars
authors: NeSmith, D.S.

title: Highbush Blueberry Cultivars Differ in the Relationship between Seed Number and Berry Weight during the Harvest Season

measured_variables: Seed number, berry size, weight through season

title: Southern Highbush Blueberry Production in High Tunnels: Temperatures, Development, Yield, and Fruit Quality During the Establishment Years
authors: Ogden, A.B.; van Iersel, M.W.
sample_size_if_known: Site replication as reported in article
measured_variables: Temperature, developmental stages, yield and fruit quality
main_supported_claim: Tunnel changed daytime/winter thermal environment and advanced development, but did not guarantee nighttime heat retention or freeze protection

title: Early Ripening of Southern Highbush Blueberries under Mild Winter Conditions
